_comment: Every number here is either MEASURED by the user (marked M), taken from the Feetech SCS0009 datasheet (D), read off the STEP/CAD (C) or a GUESS (G) that should be replaced by a measurement. Edit and re-run tools/build_model.py to regenerate model/tars.xml.
measured_leg_mass_g_src: M: one outer leg/arm on scale (photo 2)
foot_weight_g_src: M: steel stick-on balance weight 19.8 g (photo 3), one per leg
foot_weight_included_in_leg_mass_src: M: CONFIRMED by user: the 83.6 g leg includes the 20 g weight
foot_weight_size_mm_src: G: steel 19.8 g = 2.5 cm3; photo suggests ~25x18x5.5 mm
slider_servo_mass_g_src: G: ear-less hip servos assumed ~1 g lighter
unmodelled_electronics_pos_cad_mm_src: G: PCB+battery+wires lump position (CAD frame x,y,z). THE BIGGEST UNKNOWN for CoM height -> please measure real CoM.
mass_src: G: small electronics masses are estimates
robot_frame: X forward (=CAD +y, screen side), Y left (=CAD +x), Z up (=CAD -z, camera/USB-C end is the head). Origin = hip-axis centre at mid-plane (CAD x=0.6,y=1.9,z=0).
up_is_cad_minus_z_src: M: CONFIRMED by user: the head is the USB end (= CAD -z end)

servo.src: D: Feetech SCS0009 datasheet SCS0009-C013 (2.3 kg.cm @6V, 1.89 kg.cm @4.8V, 0.1 s/60deg @6V, 0.125 s/60deg @4.8V)

servo_model.src: G: internal PID gains / reflected inertia / gearbox friction are NOT in the datasheet -> fit from a logged step response

lift_crank.src: C+firmware: robot_action.cc crank-slider constants; guide friction G

foot_weight_placement: M: CONFIRMED by user: steel block lies flat at the very bottom of each leg, pushed into a slot in the printed structure (foot contact surface = steel or plastic: still to be confirmed)

firmware_facts.mcp_turn_positive_is_left: from tars_board.cc self.tars.turn description (positive = left turn) - ask user to re-confirm on the robot
firmware_facts.servo_mapping_result: rl/sign_study.py: ID1 = LEFT arm; (sig1,sig2,sig3) = (+1,-1,-1) [default hypothesis a] or all flipped [b]; hip/lift signs only determined up to one simultaneous flip -> firmware self-test

battery_supply.type: 2S Li-ion, servos powered directly from the pack (tars_board.cc GetBatteryLevel: 6.6 V empty .. 8.4 V full, read through servo ID1)
battery_supply.note: datasheet rates 4-7.4 V and gives data only at 4.8 V and 6 V; torque/speed assumed ~proportional to V (6.3-8.4 V incl. sag -> tau_range 1.0-1.4 x the 6 V figures). >7.4 V is above the rated range (over-voltage protection trips at 9 V).
